(Doris Bry [1920-2014], New York).[1] Susan and David Workman, New York.[2] (Kraushaar Galleries, New York). (Kennedy Galleries, New York, by 1977); private collection; gift 2021 to NGA. (Source: NGA, 2025) 
 
[1] The provenance is adapted from Lynes, 1999. 
 
[2] A label from the back of the painting names the couple as lenders to the 1970 retrospective exhibition at the Whitney Museum of American Art.
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. O'Keeffe wrote: "One morning the world was covered with snow. As I walked past the V of the red hills, I was startled to see them white. It was a beautiful early morning—black crows flying over the white. It became another painting—the snow–covered hills holding up the sky, a black bird flying, always there, always going away" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 86). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Anonymous Gift, 2021.58.1
description: The elegant, simplified form of a blackbird hovers at the top center of the composition above two white hills that come together in a V-shape. The sky behind the bird fades from bright blue at the top of the image to white near the horizon.
imageCaption: Courtesy of National Gallery of Art.
